name: process_rmpp_ack
prose: Precondition: agent is a registered MAD agent, mad_recv_wc holds a received RMPP ACK, and the caller does not hold agent->lock. Postcondition: it returns nothing. If the header's rmpp_status is nonzero it calls abort_send and nack_recv with IB_MGMT_RMPP_STATUS_BAD_STATUS and returns without taking the lock; if newwin < seg_num it does the same with IB_MGMT_RMPP_STATUS_W2S. Otherwise it takes agent->lock (irqsave) and looks up the send with ib_find_send_mad. With no matching send it calls process_ds_ack only when seg_num is 0, then unlocks and returns. With a matching send: if last_ack == seg_count and timeout is nonzero it unlocks and calls ack_ds_ack; if last_ack == seg_count, or timeout is 0, or the state is IB_MAD_STATE_CANCELED it unlocks and returns; if seg_num exceeds seg_count or the send's newwin it unlocks and calls abort_send and nack_recv with IB_MGMT_RMPP_STATUS_S2B; if newwin is below the send's newwin or seg_num is below last_ack (an old ACK) it unlocks and returns. Otherwise it calls adjust_last_ack and resets retries_left to max_retries when seg_num > last_ack, stores newwin in the send, and then: if last_ack == seg_count and send_buf.timeout_ms is 0 it calls ib_mark_mad_done and, if the state became IB_MAD_STATE_DONE, unlocks and completes the send with IB_WC_SUCCESS (otherwise just unlocks); if last_ack == seg_count and timeout_ms is nonzero it resets the response timeout when the state is IB_MAD_STATE_WAIT_RESP, unlocks and calls ack_ds_ack; if last_ack != seg_count and the state is IB_MAD_STATE_WAIT_RESP with the send's seg_num below newwin and seg_count, it calls send_next_seg, and only on success sets the state to IB_MAD_STATE_SEND_START and moves the send to the agent's send_list (on failure the state and list position are unchanged, but send_next_seg has already incremented seg_num and rewritten the RMPP header and timeout), then unlocks. The lock is released on every path that takes it.
note: reviewer round 15 right (send_next_seg mutates seg_num, flags and timeout before ib_send_mad, mad_rmpp.c:567-596, so 'leaves the send unchanged' was wrong); round 2 (W2B) wrong because the old prose already said W2S and the code uses W2S; round 1 already reflected (process_ds_ack only for seg_num == 0). mad_rmpp.c:652-720.

name: ib_nl_handle_set_timeout
prose: Precondition: skb and nlh are a received netlink message. Postcondition: it returns -EPERM immediately, without taking a lock or changing state, if NLM_F_REQUEST is not set in nlh->nlmsg_flags or NETLINK_CB(skb).sk is NULL. Otherwise it parses the attributes with nla_parse_deprecated; if parsing fails or the LS_NLA_TYPE_TIMEOUT attribute is absent it changes nothing. Otherwise it reads the attribute as an int, clamps it into [IB_SA_LOCAL_SVC_TIMEOUT_MIN, IB_SA_LOCAL_SVC_TIMEOUT_MAX], and under ib_nl_request_lock (irqsave) computes delta against sa_local_svc_timeout_ms; if delta is nonzero it stores the new timeout in sa_local_svc_timeout_ms, adjusts every query on ib_nl_request_list (timeout set to 0 when delta is negative and its magnitude exceeds the query's timeout, otherwise timeout += delta), and, if the list was non-empty, calls mod_delayed_work on ib_nl_timed_work with the delay derived from the first entry (at least 1). The lock is released before returning. Every path other than the -EPERM one returns 0.
note: slice cut the head; packet name ib_nl_handle_settimeout does not exist, the function is ib_nl_handle_set_timeout (sa_query.c:1049-1109). Prose from the previous round matched the code.

name: UVERBS_HANDLER(UVERBS_METHOD_REG_DMABUF_MR)
prose: Generated function (UVERBS_HANDLER macro expands to the method's handler name) for UVERBS_METHOD_REG_DMABUF_MR(attrs). Precondition: attrs is the attribute bundle of a REG_DMABUF_MR call with the mandatory handle, PD handle and value attributes present. Postcondition: it returns -EOPNOTSUPP if the PD's device has no reg_user_mr_dmabuf op; otherwise it reads offset, length and iova with uverbs_copy_from (returning the error), returns -EINVAL if the page offsets of offset and iova differ, reads the fd with uverbs_copy_from and the access flags with uverbs_get_flags32 (returning either error), returns the error of ib_check_mr_access, and calls the device's reg_user_mr_dmabuf, returning PTR_ERR of an error pointer. On success of that call it initialises mr (device, pd, type IB_MR_TYPE_USER, uobject), increments pd->usecnt, adds the MR to restrack, sets uobj->object and finalises the uobject, then copies lkey and rkey to the response attributes and returns 0, or the error of a failing uverbs_copy_to (in which case the MR has already been finalised and the function does not itself destroy it).
note: reviewer round 15 claim (uverbs_get_raw_fd failure path) is wrong: this function reads the fd with uverbs_copy_from, there is no uverbs_get_raw_fd call (uverbs_std_types_mr.c, UVERBS_METHOD_REG_DMABUF_MR handler head at line 186). Dropped the unverified precondition about the write lock and the claim that no references leak.

name: UVERBS_HANDLER(UVERBS_METHOD_QP_CREATE)
prose: Generated function (UVERBS_HANDLER macro) for UVERBS_METHOD_QP_CREATE(attrs). Precondition: attrs is the bundle of a QP create call with the mandatory handle, cap, user-handle and type attributes. Postcondition: it returns the error of reading the cap, user handle or QP type. By QP type it validates the attribute combination: for IB_QPT_XRC_TGT it returns -EINVAL if any CQ, PD or indirection-table handle is present, the error of the XRCD lookup, or -EINVAL if the XRCD object is NULL; for RAW_PACKET it returns -EPERM without the raw capability; for the other supported types it returns -EINVAL for a forbidden XRCD or SRQ combination or the error of the PD, send CQ or receive CQ lookups (and -EINVAL when an indirection table is used together with receive resources); any other type gives -EINVAL. It then returns the error of reading the create flags, of check_creation_flags and of reading the source QPN, and -EINVAL when an SRQ's type does not match an XRC target. After that it takes the async event file reference with ib_uverbs_get_async_event and calls ib_create_qp_user; if that fails it drops the event file reference (if one was acquired) and returns the error. On success it increments the QP usecount, for XRC_TGT takes a reference on the XRCD's uxrcd, sets the uobject's object, finalises the uobject, and copies the response caps and QP number, returning 0 or the error of either copy. A failure of those copies returns after the QP uobject has been finalised, without dropping the event file reference.
note: reviewer (round 15) is right: the event-file reference is dropped only on ib_create_qp_user failure (err_put); a copy_to failure after finalisation returns without that cleanup. uverbs_std_types_qp.c:82-284 (head at line 82, slice cut the head).

name: bnxt_qplib_create_qp
prose: Precondition: res and qp are valid with res->rcfw, res->dattr and res->cctx usable, qp->scq, qp->rcq, qp->pd and qp->dpi valid (qp->srq valid if set), and the SQ and (when qp->srq is NULL) RQ sg_info/size attributes prepared; the caller does not hold rcfw->tbl_lock. Postcondition: it allocates the SQ hardware queue (returning its error at once if that allocation fails), the SQ software queue unless the SQ is user-owned, the RQ hardware and software queues unless qp->srq is set, and, when the QP type is RC (psn_sz nonzero), the ORRQ and IRRQ hardware queues (these have no software queues). It then sends the CREATE_QP command with bnxt_qplib_rcfw_send_message. On success it returns 0 with qp->id from the firmware response, qp->cur_qp_state set to CMDQ_MODIFY_QP_NEW_STATE_RESET, the flush lists initialised, the SQ dbinfo (and the RQ dbinfo when rq->max_wqe is nonzero) filled in, and the QP stored in rcfw->qp_tbl under spin_lock_bh(&rcfw->tbl_lock), which is released before return; all allocated queues stay allocated for the caller. On any failure it returns the negative errno of the failing step and the QP is not registered; the queues allocated before the failing step are freed (a failing send frees the IRRQ, ORRQ, RQ software and hardware queues and the SQ software and hardware queues; an earlier failure frees only the ones already allocated, e.g. an IRRQ allocation failure frees the ORRQ and the earlier queues).
note: reviewer (round 15) is right: ORRQ and IRRQ are allocated with bnxt_qplib_alloc_init_hwq only, no software queue (qplib_fp.c create_qp at 958-1190); old prose also overstated the cleanup as always releasing everything in reverse order.

name: bnxt_qplib_post_send
prose: Precondition: qp and wqe are valid, with the SQ hardware queue and dbinfo initialised. Postcondition: it returns -EINVAL, without touching the SQ, if qp->state is neither CMDQ_MODIFY_QP_NEW_STATE_RTS nor CMDQ_MODIFY_QP_NEW_STATE_ERR, and -ENOMEM, without touching the SQ, if the SQ cannot hold the required slots plus qdf. Otherwise it takes the next swq entry, calls bnxt_qplib_pull_psn_buff (this happens before the ERR-state test, so it also runs for ERR), and fills the swq's slot_idx, slots, wr_id, type, flags (plus SIGNAL_COMP when qp->sig_type is set) and start_psn. If qp->state is ERR it skips all header encoding and PSN handling, starts the swq, advances the SQ producer by swq->slots, increments qp->wqe_cnt and then tries to schedule bnxt_qpn_cqn_sched_task work on the send CQ's NQ with a GFP_ATOMIC allocation, returning -ENOMEM (after the WQE has already been queued) if that allocation fails and 0 otherwise. In RTS state it zeroes the two header slots, writes the SGEs or inline data and returns -EINVAL if the data length exceeds BNXT_RE_MAX_MSG_SIZE or the WQE type is unknown (in both cases the producer, wqe_cnt and sq->psn are not advanced, though swq metadata and some queue slots were written). For known types it encodes the headers and advances sq->psn by the packet count for RC sends, RDMA read/write and atomics, by 1 for UD/GSI sends, and not for the GSI raw-Ethernet SEND, LOCAL_INV, FAST_REG_MR and BIND_MW; unless the MSN table is host-owned and the WQE type does not update it (UD/GSI sends, LOCAL_INV, FAST_REG_MR, BIND_MW), it sets swq->next_psn and fills the PSN search entry. It then starts the swq, advances the producer, increments qp->wqe_cnt and returns 0.
note: reviewers right on points that the old prose already had or got wrong: the SQ-full path returns -ENOMEM; pull_psn_buff is also called on the ERR path (round 15); GSI raw SEND does not advance psn (round 2). Old prose put the -ENOMEM from nq_work allocation correctly; rewritten for clarity. qplib_fp.c:1851-1973.

name: bnxt_qplib_cq_process_terminal
prose: Precondition: cq is a valid CQ, hwcqe points to a terminal CQE, and pcqe and budget point to the caller's CQE cursor and remaining budget. Postcondition: it warns if hwcqe->status is not CQ_TERMINAL_STATUS_OK. If the CQE's qp_handle decodes to NULL it returns -EINVAL without changing the QP; otherwise it sets qp->state to CMDQ_MODIFY_QP_NEW_STATE_ERR. If sq_cons_idx is not 0xFFFF and the SQ is not already flushed, it walks the SQ from sq->swq_last toward sq_cons_idx % sq->max_sw_wqe while *budget is nonzero, writing a zeroed status-OK request CQE for each swq entry with SQ_SEND_FLAGS_SIGNAL_COMP (advancing *pcqe and decrementing *budget) and advancing the SQ consumer and sq->swq_last for every entry visited; if *budget reaches 0 and the index of the last visited entry (0 if none was visited) differs from the target it returns -EAGAIN, without examining the RQ or adding the QP to the flush list, and this includes the case where the last entry visited was the final one before the target. Otherwise (and when the SQ is skipped) it examines the RQ: it returns 0 if rq_cons_idx is 0xFFFF or the RQ is flushed, returns -EINVAL if rq_cons_idx exceeds rq->max_wqe - 1, and otherwise calls bnxt_qplib_add_flush_qp(qp) and returns 0.
note: reviewer round 15 wrong: with budget exhausted right after processing the last entry before the target, swq_last still holds the processed index (it differs from cqe_cons) so the function returns -EAGAIN, as the old prose said (qplib_fp.c, loop at 'while (*budget)' and 'if (!(*budget) && swq_last != cqe_cons)'); round 2 (local swq_last) and round 1 (flush list conditional) are consistent with the old prose. Added the SQ-flushed skip and the status warning.

name: peer_abort
prose: Precondition: dev and skb are valid and skb carries a CPL abort request. Postcondition: it always returns 0. If get_ep_from_tid finds no endpoint it returns at once. Otherwise, if the abort status is negative advice it only increments the endpoint and device negative-advice counters and goes to the final two c4iw_put_ep calls. Otherwise it sets PEER_ABORT in the endpoint history, wakes wr_waitp with -ECONNRESET unless the state is MPA_REQ_SENT, and under ep->com.mutex acts by state: CONNECTING puts the parent endpoint; MPA_REQ_WAIT stops the timer; MPA_REQ_SENT stops the timer and either calls connect_reply_upcall(-ECONNRESET) or, when retrying with MPA v1, sets retry_with_mpa_v1; MORIBUND/CLOSING stop the timer and fall into FPDU_MODE handling, which for an SRQ-backed QP either completes cached SRQ buffers or takes an extra ref, sets ABORTING and calls read_tcb, and otherwise moves the QP to ERROR (if cm_id and qp exist) and calls peer_abort_upcall; MPA_REP_SENT, MPA_REQ_RCVD and ABORTING do nothing special; DEAD warns, unlocks and skips to the final puts without sending a reply; any other state triggers WARN_ONCE. After the switch it calls dst_confirm and, if the state is not ABORTING, sets it to DEAD and sets release unless retry_with_mpa_v1. It then dequeues a reply skb (if none, WARN, release is set and no reply is sent), builds and sends the abort reply, and then either releases the endpoint resources (release set) or, if retry_with_mpa_v1, releases the CLIP, tid, dst and l2t resources and calls c4iw_reconnect; with ABORTING and no retry it does neither. It always ends with two c4iw_put_ep calls on the endpoint.
note: reviewer (round 15) is right: in the ABORTING case with no MPA retry neither the release nor the mpa_v1 cleanup runs; old prose said 'either'. Slice cut the head (function starts at cm.c:2816). Enumerated the state switch and the DEAD and missing-reply exits.

name: write_adapter_mem
prose: Precondition: rdev is a valid c4iw_rdev, addr is a 32-byte-aligned adapter address, skb is NULL or a valid buffer, and data and wr_waitp satisfy the requirements of whichever helper is selected. Postcondition: it returns _c4iw_write_mem_inline(rdev, addr, len, data, skb, wr_waitp) when rdev->lldi.ulptx_memwrite_dsgl is 0, or the module parameter use_dsgl is 0, or len <= inline_threshold; otherwise it returns _c4iw_write_mem_dma(rdev, addr, len, data, skb, wr_waitp). It does nothing itself beyond that choice; the return value and the handling of data, skb and wr_waitp (including the documented behaviour that a NULL data means 'zero len bytes') are those of the selected helper.
note: all three reviewer complaints are about helper behaviour (wr_waitp NULL, zeroing in the DMA path), which the old prose attributed to this function; the function only dispatches (cxgb4/mem.c:231-244). Reduced to the dispatch and removed claims about the helpers that cannot be verified here.

name: create_qp
prose: Precondition: rdev, wq, rcq, scq and wr_waitp are valid, uctx is rdev->uctx for a kernel QP or a user context for a user QP, wq->sq.size (and wq->rq.size when need_rq) are set. Postcondition: it allocates a qid for the SQ with c4iw_get_qpid, and for the RQ when need_rq is set, returning -ENOMEM if a qid cannot be allocated; for a kernel QP it allocates the software SQ (and RQ when need_rq) arrays with kcalloc (-ENOMEM on failure), for need_rq allocates an RQT pool entry of a power-of-two size of at least 16 (-ENOMEM on failure), allocates the SQ with alloc_sq (its error on failure), allocates the RQ DMA buffer with dma_alloc_coherent (-ENOMEM), looks up the BAR2 addresses and returns -EINVAL for a user QP whose SQ or RQ BAR2 address is missing, allocates an skb (-ENOMEM), builds a FW_RI_RES_WR for the SQ (and RQ) and sends it with c4iw_ref_send_wait, returning that error on failure. On success it returns 0 with the qids, software queues, RQT entry and DMA queues left allocated for the caller. On any failure it unwinds, in reverse order, what it had allocated up to that point: RQ DMA buffer, SQ, RQT entry, software RQ and SQ arrays, RQ qid and SQ qid.
note: slice cut the head; packet name create_wq does not exist, the function is create_qp (cxgb4/qp.c:199-412). Old prose wrongly said the qids were allocated by the caller (it allocates them with c4iw_get_qpid) and omitted the qid, software-queue and RQT failure paths.

name: erdma_create_qp
prose: Precondition: ibqp is an erdma_qp in an erdma device; attrs describes the requested QP; udata is NULL for a kernel QP or valid user data (uctx non-NULL). Postcondition: it returns the error of erdma_qp_validate_cap or erdma_qp_validate_attr without allocating or registering anything. Otherwise it sets scq, rcq, dev and cc, initialises state_lock, the kref and safe_free, and registers the QP in dev->qp_xa (under id 1 for IB_QPT_GSI, otherwise a cyclic id in [1, max_qp - 1]); any failure of that registration returns -ENOMEM with the QP not registered. It rounds sq_size and rq_size up to powers of two and, for a user QP, copies the request (error returned), calls init_user_qp, fills the response and copies it out with ib_copy_to_udata; for a kernel QP it calls init_kernel_qp. A failure of init_user_qp or init_kernel_qp erases the QP from dev->qp_xa and returns its error without calling free_user_qp or free_kernel_qp, and a failure of ib_copy_to_udata or of create_qp_cmd calls free_user_qp or free_kernel_qp and then erases the QP from dev->qp_xa before returning the error. On success it sets max_send_sge, max_recv_sge, the initial iWARP or RoCEv2 state, arms the reflush delayed work, issues create_qp_cmd, initialises qp->lock and returns 0.
note: reviewer (round 15) is right: the init_user_qp and init_kernel_qp failures go to err_out_xa, skipping the free_user_qp/free_kernel_qp calls, so the old 'any queue memory already set up is freed' claim was wrong for those two paths (erdma_verbs.c:992-1043, labels err_out_cmd/err_out_xa/err_out). Slice cut the head.

name: hfi1_init_dd
prose: Precondition: dd is a hfi1_devdata for a PCI device whose pcidev and port structures are set; called once at probe. Postcondition: it initialises the per-port defaults and then runs the chip bring-up in order: hfi1_pcie_ddinit, save_pci_variables, optional check_int_registers, init_asic_data, init_chip, pcie_speeds, eprom_init, firmware init, the PCIe Gen3 transition, obtain_boardname, hfi1_alloc_rx, context variables, RXE, send contexts, kernel contexts, per-VL send contexts, SDMA init per port, set_up_interrupts, completion vectors, load_firmware, thermal_init (its result is not checked), counters, init_rcverr, user_comp and finally sets dd->user_refcount to 1. It returns 0 on that path. On a failure it returns that step's error: a failure of hfi1_pcie_ddinit returns with no cleanup; most failures up to set_up_interrupts free the rx data and PCIe state (hfi1_free_rx, hfi1_pcie_ddcleanup); failures of hfi1_comp_vectors_set_up and load_firmware also release the completion vectors and MSI-X interrupts; a failure of init_cntrs does the same; a failure of init_rcverr also frees the counters; and an eprom_init failure takes the longest unwind, which additionally calls free_rcverr and free_cntrs even though those had not been set up.
note: slice cut the head; packet name unnamed_device_init does not exist, the function is hfi1_init_dd (hfi1/chip.c:14975-15307). Reviewer (round 15) is right that thermal_init's result is ignored, and 'unwinding exactly the resources acquired so far' was inaccurate for eprom_init failures (goto bail_free_rcverr).

name: def_access_sw_cpu(cntr)
prose: Generated function access_sw_cpu_<cntr> from the def_access_sw_cpu macro (instantiated for rc_acks, rc_qacks and rc_delayed_comp): access_sw_cpu_<cntr>(entry, context, vl, mode, data). Precondition: context is a valid struct hfi1_pportdata pointer whose dd and ibport_data.rvp counters exist. Postcondition: it returns read_write_cpu(ppd->dd, &ppd->ibport_data.rvp.z_<cntr>, ppd->ibport_data.rvp.<cntr>, vl, mode, data), where the macro parameter is substituted in both places. read_write_cpu returns 0 if vl is not CNTR_INVALID_VL; in CNTR_MODE_R mode it returns the sum of the per-CPU counter minus the saved zero value; in CNTR_MODE_W mode it sets the saved zero value to the current sum when data is 0 (a nonzero data only logs an error) and returns 0; for any other mode it logs an error and returns 0. The entry argument is unused.
note: slice cut the head; name is the macro head at hfi1/chip.c:4051-4059. Reviewer (round 15) is wrong: the macro text rvp.cntr is a macro parameter and is substituted like z_ ##cntr, so the third argument is the per-CPU counter named by cntr.

name: do_pcie_gen3_transition
prose: Precondition: dd is a valid, initialised hfi1_devdata. Postcondition: it returns 0 without doing anything if dd->icode is not ICODE_RTL_SILICON, if pcie_target is not 1, 2 or 3, if the link is already at the target speed and pcie_force is not set, or if there is no upstream bridge. For a Gen3 target on a link that is not Gen3 capable it logs an error and ends with ret = -ENOSYS, which is returned as 0 (it is not a fatal error, see below). It returns the error of acquire_chip_resource(CR_SBUS) at once if the SBus cannot be taken. Otherwise it disables thermal polling, then loops (up to pcie_retry extra attempts when the link does not reach the target speed or width): download the SBus and PCIe firmware (load_pcie_firmware), program the PCIe port-logic registers, load the EQ table (load_eq_table), program gasket interrupts, set the target link speed on the parent and the device, trigger a secondary bus reset (trigger_sbr), check the VendorID, restore PCI variables, check the gasket status and errors and refresh the link speed and width. At the end it re-enables thermal polling and releases the SBus resource. Any failure is converted to a return value of 0 (continue at the current speed) unless return_error was set; return_error is set, and the error returned, for a firmware download failure, a failed read or write of the link control 2 register on parent or device, a failed or all-ones VendorID read after the reset (-EIO for all ones), a failed restore_pci_variables, a first gasket status read of all ones (-ENOSYS) and a failed read of the lane-error register. Failures of load_eq_table, trigger_sbr, an unexpected gasket status or error (-EIO) and a link that still does not match after the retries are therefore returned as 0.
note: slice cut the head; packet name unnamed_pcie_gen3_transition_function does not exist, the function is do_pcie_gen3_transition (hfi1/pcie.c:932-1382). The earlier dropped prose claimed the listed errors are returned, but most are swallowed by the 'Proceeding at current speed' conversion at done_no_mutex.

name: do_pcie_gen3_transition
prose: Precondition: dd is a valid, initialised hfi1_devdata. Postcondition: it returns 0 without doing anything if dd->icode is not ICODE_RTL_SILICON, if pcie_target is not 1, 2 or 3, if the link is already at the target speed and pcie_force is not set, or if there is no upstream bridge. note: slice cut the head (this slice is the tail of the same function as record 13); packet name pcie_speed_set_tail does not exist.

name: qsfp_dump
prose: Precondition: ppd is a valid hfi1_pportdata, buf is a writable buffer of len bytes. Postcondition: it returns the number of characters written to buf (never more than len - 1 for len > 0, since each piece is added with scnprintf). If ppd->qsfp_info.cache_valid is false it writes nothing and returns 0. Otherwise it writes the lines PWR (from the power class), TECH (with a length such as '2M ' only for copper modules), Vendor, OUI, Part#, Rev, Atten (only for copper modules, QSFP_IS_CU), Serial, Date and Lot, and then a hex dump of the first QSFP_DEFAULT_HDR_CNT bytes of the cache in QSFP_DUMP_CHUNK-byte rows.
note: slice cut the head; packet name qsfp_format_mod does not exist, the function is qsfp_dump (hfi1/qsfp.c:728-796). Old prose omitted the cache_valid check and listed the wrong fields.

name: hfi1_rc_send_complete
prose: Precondition: the caller holds qp->s_lock with interrupts disabled (lockdep_assert_held) and opah is the header of a packet just sent on qp. Postcondition: it returns nothing. It returns at once if ib_rvt_state_ops[qp->state] lacks RVT_SEND_OR_FLUSH_OR_RECV_OK. If the opcode is in [RDMA_READ_RESPONSE_FIRST, ATOMIC_ACKNOWLEDGE] or is TID READ_RESP or WRITE_RESP it does WARN_ON on a zero qp->s_rdma_ack_cnt, decrements it and returns; nothing else below happens for these opcodes. Otherwise it takes the BTH psn and, unless the opcode is TID WRITE_DATA, WRITE_DATA_LAST, ACK or RESYNC, calls reset_sending_psn(qp, psn) (which scans from qp->s_last to qp->s_tail for the first WQE with lpsn >= psn and sets s_sending_psn to that WQE's lpsn + 1 if its opcode is RDMA_READ, TID_RDMA_READ or TID_RDMA_WRITE and to psn + 1 otherwise; it leaves s_sending_psn unchanged if no WQE qualifies). For opcodes from TID WRITE_REQ through WRITE_DATA_LAST it takes head = priv->s_tid_head and tail = priv->s_tid_cur, and when head == tail with an incomplete TID request at tail it moves tail back one entry, wrapping from 0 to qp->s_size - 1; for other opcodes head = qp->s_tail and tail = qp->s_acked. If psn has IB_BTH_REQ_ACK, tail != head, the opcode is not TID WRITE_DATA, WRITE_DATA_LAST or RESYNC, none of RVT_S_TIMER, RVT_S_WAIT_RNR and RVT_S_WAIT_PSN is set in s_flags and the state has RVT_PROCESS_RECV_OK, it starts the extended retry timer for TID READ_REQ and the normal retry timer otherwise. For TID WRITE_DATA, WRITE_DATA_LAST or RESYNC with IB_BTH_REQ_ACK set, HFI1_S_TID_RETRY_TIMER clear and RVT_PROCESS_RECV_OK, it starts the TID retry timer when the WQE at s_acked is IB_WR_TID_RDMA_WRITE with ack_seg < cur_seg. It then completes WQEs from qp->s_last (trdma_clean_swqe, rvt_qp_complete_swqe with IB_WC_SUCCESS) until s_last == s_acked or the WQE at s_last has lpsn >= s_sending_psn while s_sending_psn <= s_sending_hpsn. Finally, if RVT_S_WAIT_PSN is set and s_sending_psn > s_sending_hpsn, it clears RVT_S_WAIT_PSN, sets s_sending_psn to s_psn, s_sending_hpsn to s_psn - 1 and calls hfi1_schedule_send.
note: reviewers right on two points: response opcodes return early so none of the later actions apply (already stated in the old prose), and tail wraps from 0 to s_size - 1 rather than simply being decremented (round 15, rc.c:2416-2421 in this function); round 2's lpsn + 1 vs psn + 1 distinction was already in the old prose. rc.c:1690-1767.

name: hfi1_rc_rcv
prose: Precondition: packet describes a received RC packet for packet->qp, and the caller holds qp->r_lock (lockdep_assert_held); it does not hold qp->s_lock. Postcondition: it returns nothing. It returns at once if hfi1_ruc_check_hdr rejects the packet. Otherwise it processes ECN (fecn) and the OPFN connection request, and for response opcodes (RDMA_READ_RESPONSE_FIRST through ATOMIC_ACKNOWLEDGE) it calls rc_rcv_resp and returns. For a PSN that differs from qp->r_psn it calls rc_rcv_error, returning if that returns nonzero and otherwise sending an ACK (hfi1_send_rc_ack). For the expected PSN it checks that the opcode follows qp->r_state (otherwise nack_inv), calls rvt_comm_est if the QP is in RTR and not yet COMM_EST, and handles the opcode: SEND and RDMA WRITE opcodes consume an RWQE with rvt_get_rwqe where required (a negative result goes to the operational-error NAK path, zero to the RNR NAK path), copy the payload into qp->r_sge, validate tlen, access flags (IB_ACCESS_REMOTE_WRITE) and rkeys (rvt_rkey_ok, failing to the access-error path) and, on the last packet, post a receive completion with rvt_recv_cq (including immediate data or invalidate handling). For RDMA_READ_REQUEST and COMPARE_SWAP/FETCH_ADD it takes qp->s_lock (irqsave) around the ack-queue update and releases it before returning or before jumping to the _unlck NAK labels; with an OPFN atomic request it handles the OPFN response and skips the rkey check and the atomic operation. Unknown opcodes go to nack_inv. On normal completion it advances qp->r_psn, sets r_state, r_ack_psn and clears r_nak_state, and then sends an immediate ACK (rc_cancel_ack and hfi1_send_rc_ack) when an ACK was requested and numpkt is 0, fecn is set, or r_adefered reached HFI1_PSN_CREDIT, otherwise defers the ACK (rc_defered_ack). Error labels set r_nak_state and r_ack_psn: rnr_nak queues an RNR NAK; nack_op_err calls rvt_rc_error(IB_WC_LOC_QP_OP_ERR) and queues an operational-error NAK; nack_inv(_unlck) calls rvt_rc_error(IB_WC_LOC_QP_OP_ERR) and queues an invalid-request NAK; nack_acc(_unlck) calls rvt_rc_error(IB_WC_LOC_PROT_ERR) and sends the NAK immediately through the send_ack label. qp->s_lock is not held on any return.
note: slice cut the head; real function hfi1_rc_rcv (hfi1/rc.c:2755-3207); the old prose said NAKs are 'sent' and that the caller must not hold qp->s_lock only; the code asserts qp->r_lock and queues most NAKs with rc_defered_ack. Reviewer (round 15) right that the OPFN atomic case skips the rkey check and the atomic operation.

name: hfi1_make_rc_req
prose: Precondition: the caller holds qp->s_lock (lockdep_assert_held) and ps is the packet state. Postcondition: it returns 1 when a packet or work item was handled and 0 when nothing could be sent. It first obtains a tx request with get_txreq; if that fails it goes to the no-tx exit. If RVT_S_RESP_PENDING is set and make_rc_ack builds a response it returns 1 with the response in ps->s_txreq. If the QP state does not allow sending it either bails out or, in a flushing state with queued WQEs and no pending SDMA, completes the WQE at s_last with hfi1_trdma_send_complete and returns 1 after freeing the tx request (it sets RVT_S_WAIT_DMA and bails when SDMA is pending). It bails (return 0) when RNR, ACK or HALT waits are set, when s_psn is still within the sending window (setting RVT_S_WAIT_PSN), when the send queue is empty, when a fence or TID interlock blocks the WQE (setting RVT_S_WAIT_FENCE for a fence), when no credit is available, or when a TID request limit is reached. A local operation (IB_WR_REG_MR or LOCAL_INV) at the head is completed immediately and the function returns 1 after freeing the tx request. Otherwise it builds exactly one request or retransmitted packet from the WQE at s_cur according to the opcode (send, RDMA write, TID RDMA write/read, RDMA read, atomic), updates s_state, s_psn, s_cur, s_lsn, s_num_rd_atomic and the TID fields, fills the packet header with hfi1_make_ruc_header and returns 1 with the packet in ps->s_txreq. The 0 return (bail and no-tx exits) releases the tx request if one was obtained, sets ps->s_txreq to NULL, clears RVT_S_BUSY and sets IOWAIT_PENDING_IB; it does not build a packet.
note: reviewer (round 15) is right: the old prose had the return values inverted; 1 is returned when a response, a request packet, or a completed flush/local WQE (tx request freed) results, and 0 only on the bail exits (hfi1/rc.c:785-1177; returns at 'return 1', 'done_free_tx' and 'bail'). Summary kept at the level that was checked line by line; the per-opcode details are not enumerated.

name: hfi1_rc_rcv_tid_rdma_read_resp
prose: Precondition: packet is a received TID RDMA READ RESPONSE for packet->qp; the caller does not hold qp->s_lock. Postcondition: it returns nothing. It computes fecn, kpsn (BTH psn) and the verbs psn ipsn, takes qp->s_lock (irqsave) and releases it on every exit. If find_tid_request(qp, ipsn, IB_WR_TID_RDMA_READ) finds no request it goes to ack_op_err; and that path, and the length-check failures below, call rvt_error_qp(qp, IB_WC_WR_FLUSH_ERR) only when qp->s_last == qp->s_acked. If ipsn differs from flow->flow_state.ib_lpsn it calls update_r_next_psn_fecn and, if kpsn differs from flow->flow_state.r_next_psn, returns without further change (duplicate or out-of-order packet); if kpsn matches it sets r_next_psn to kpsn + 1 and, for a FECN eager packet, goes to ack_op_err when tlen != hdrsize + pmtu + extra_bytes or restart_sge returns less than pmtu, otherwise copies pmtu bytes into the request's SGE with rvt_copy_sge and sets HFI1_R_TID_SW_PSN; in this branch ack_pending, pending_tid_r_segs and s_num_rd_atomic are not decremented. If ipsn equals ib_lpsn it sets r_next_psn to kpsn + 1, decrements req->ack_pending, priv->pending_tid_r_segs and qp->s_num_rd_atomic, clears RVT_S_WAIT_FENCE and RVT_S_WAIT_ACK and schedules a send only if RVT_S_WAIT_FENCE was set and s_num_rd_atomic is now 0, separately clears RVT_S_WAIT_RDMAR and RVT_S_WAIT_ACK and schedules a send if RVT_S_WAIT_RDMAR was set, releases the request's TID resources with hfi1_kern_exp_rcv_clear, and calls do_rc_ack; if that returns zero it finishes without further changes, otherwise it increments req->comp_seg (setting the request TID_REQUEST_COMPLETE and incrementing priv->tid_r_comp when comp_seg reaches total_segs), clears the hardware flow and HFI1_R_TID_SW_PSN and moves a SYNC request back to ACTIVE when the sync point is reached or tid_r_comp equals tid_r_reqs, and schedules a send.
note: reviewers rounds 1-15 right on details the old prose blurred: WAIT_FENCE is cleared only when s_num_rd_atomic is 0 (round 15), the duplicate/out-of-order path ends without error (round 1), and the ipsn != ib_lpsn path advances r_next_psn without the decrements (round 2). hfi1/tid_rdma.c:2440-2582.

name: hfi1_uc_rcv
prose: Precondition: packet describes a received UC packet for packet->qp. Postcondition: it returns nothing. It returns at once if hfi1_ruc_check_hdr rejects the packet. Otherwise, if the packet PSN differs from qp->r_psn it sets qp->r_psn to the packet PSN and drops any current message (setting RVT_R_REWIND_SGE and clearing r_sge.num_sge when the previous state was SEND_FIRST or SEND_MIDDLE, otherwise rvt_put_ss), sets r_state to SEND_LAST, and continues as a first packet for SEND_FIRST, SEND_ONLY, SEND_ONLY_WITH_IMMEDIATE and the RDMA WRITE first/only opcodes, and drops the packet (increments ibp->rvp.n_pkt_drops) for any other opcode. Otherwise it checks the opcode against qp->r_state (an unexpected one goes to the same resync path as a PSN error), calls rvt_comm_est if the QP is in RTR and not COMM_EST, and handles the opcode: SEND first/only packets take an RWQE with rvt_get_rwqe (negative: rvt_rc_error(IB_WC_LOC_QP_OP_ERR); zero: drop), middle packets copy data after length checks (a bad length sets RVT_R_REWIND_SGE and drops), and last packets complete the receive with a work completion (rvt_recv_cq); RDMA WRITE packets check IB_ACCESS_REMOTE_WRITE and the rkey (failure drops), copy data with rvt_copy_sge, and RDMA WRITE LAST/ONLY WITH IMMEDIATE also consume an RWQE and post a completion. Unknown opcodes and length errors drop the packet. On success it increments qp->r_psn and sets qp->r_state to the opcode. It takes no lock itself.
note: slice cut the head; packet name __process_rcv_packet (RC receive path) does not exist, the function is hfi1_uc_rcv (hfi1/uc.c:251-542), the UC receive handler. The earlier drop was wrong.

name: hfi1_user_exp_rcv_setup
prose: Precondition: fd is a valid hfi1_filedata with fd->uctxt, fd->tid_lock and tid_limit set up and tinfo points to a hfi1_tid_info whose tidlist is a user buffer large enough for the TIDs. Postcondition: it returns -EINVAL if tinfo->vaddr is not page aligned or tinfo->length is 0, and -ENOMEM if the tidbuf or its psets array cannot be allocated. When fd->use_mn it inserts an MMU interval notifier (returning its error). It pins the user pages (a negative result from pin_rcv_pages is returned, and zero pages gives -ENOSPC), finds physically contiguous page sets, and reserves min(n_psets, tid_limit - tid_used) TIDs under fd->tid_lock (-ENOSPC if none can be reserved), allocates the tidlist (-ENOMEM on failure), and under uctxt->exp_mutex programs whole free groups and then partially used groups with program_rcvarray. If nothing was programmed it returns the negative error of program_rcvarray or -ENOSPC. If at least one TID was programmed, a later negative error from program_rcvarray is ignored and the setup continues with the TIDs programmed so far. It then returns reserved-but-unused TIDs to fd->tid_used, unpins the pages not covered by a TID, and with fd->use_mn returns -EBUSY if an invalidation occurred during setup; it sets tinfo->tidcnt and tinfo->length = mapped_pages * PAGE_SIZE, and returns -EFAULT if copy_to_user of the TID list fails. On success it removes the notifier, frees pages, psets, tidbuf and tidlist and returns 0. On the -EBUSY and -EFAULT failures it clears the programmed TIDs (hfi1_user_exp_rcv_clear, with its result ignored and tinfo->tidlist set to 0 afterwards), and on all failures it undoes the fd->tid_used reservation, removes the notifier and unpins pages that are still pinned, and frees the tidbuf arrays, tidbuf and tidlist.
note: reviewer (round 15) is right: a negative program_rcvarray result is returned only when no TID was programmed (tididx == 0); otherwise the function proceeds and can return 0. name was outside slice (head at hfi1/user_exp_rcv.c:197).

name: dlid_to_selector
prose: Precondition: none; dlid is a u16. Postcondition: it returns a selector in 0..255 for dlid: on first use it fills the function's static 256-byte mapping table with 0xFF; it hashes dlid to ((dlid >> 8) ^ dlid) & 0xFF and, if that mapping entry is still 0xFF, assigns it the static counter value next and advances next as (next + 1) & 0x7F; it then returns the mapping entry. It keeps state in static variables and has no locking, so concurrent callers can race.
note: slice cut the head; real name dlid_to_selector (hfi1/user_sdma.c:249-268). The earlier drop was wrong: this is a real function. Note: an entry can still hold 0xFF only if never assigned; assigned values are at most 0x7F.

name: to_ionic_qp_type
prose: Precondition: type is an enum ib_qp_type value. Postcondition: it returns IONIC_QPT_UD for IB_QPT_GSI or IB_QPT_UD, IONIC_QPT_RC for IB_QPT_RC, IONIC_QPT_UC for IB_QPT_UC, IONIC_QPT_XRC_INI for IB_QPT_XRC_INI, IONIC_QPT_XRC_TGT for IB_QPT_XRC_TGT (in the enum, RC=0, UC=1, UD=3, XRC_INI=5, XRC_TGT=6), and -EINVAL for every other type. It has no side effects.

name: irdma_modify_qp
prose: Precondition: ibqp is an irdma QP, attr and attr_mask describe the change, udata is NULL or user data, and the caller may sleep (the function waits on iwqp->mod_qp_waitq for pending hardware modifies). Postcondition: it returns -EINVAL if udata has a nonzero inlen below the minimum request length or a nonzero outlen below the minimum response length, and -EOPNOTSUPP if attr_mask has a bit outside IB_QP_ATTR_STANDARD_BITS. Under iwqp->lock it handles IB_QP_STATE: INIT or RTR return -EINVAL when iwarp_state is above IDLE (and request IDLE and possibly a push page); RTS returns -EINVAL if iwarp_state is above RTS or there is no cm_id; SQD returns 0 with no change if hw_iwarp_state is above RTS or iwarp_state is CLOSING or below RTS, and -EINVAL above CLOSING; SQE returns -EINVAL at or above TERMINATE; ERR and RESET, when iwarp_state is already ERROR, set iwqp->ibqp_state, unlock, optionally copy the flush request from udata (returning -EINVAL if that copy fails, after ibqp_state changed) and flush the WQEs, then return 0; otherwise they delete the terminate timer if term_flags is set and request ERROR; any other qp_state returns -EINVAL. Accepted states set iwqp->ibqp_state. Access flags update the offload info and the QP context is written when marked valid. The lock is dropped; if a hardware modify was requested, a failure of irdma_hw_modify_qp returns -EINVAL, and otherwise iwqp->iwarp_state is updated only if it still equals the value seen when the lock was held. If a hardware modify was issued and ibqp_state is above IB_QPS_RTS it calls irdma_cm_disconn (marking the TCP state closed first when dont_wait is set and hw_tcp_state is nonzero) or, when dont_wait is 0 and a cm_node exists, starts the close timer once. Finally for IB_QP_STATE with udata->outlen on hardware generation 2 or later it may set up push mmap entries and copies the response, returning the error of ib_copy_to_udata after removing the push mmap entries; otherwise it returns 0. iwqp->lock is released on every return.
note: second pass of an unreviewed prose: removed the unverified 'flushes WQEs when ibqp_state is above RTS' claim (the flush is not in this function except on the ERR/RESET already-ERROR path) and added the conditional iwarp_state update and the -EINVAL from irdma_hw_modify_qp; reviewers rounds 1 and 2 (SQD no-op returns 0, copy failure after ibqp_state changed, input validation) are consistent with the code. irdma/verbs.c:1633-1782.

name: aliasguid_query_handler
prose: Precondition: context is NULL or a valid mlx4_alias_guid_work_context; when status is 0, guid_rec points to the SA response. Postcondition: it returns nothing and returns at once if context is NULL. Otherwise, if status is nonzero it sets the record's time_to_run to one second from now and skips to the requeue step; if guid_rec->block_num differs from cb_ctx->block_num it logs an error and also skips to the requeue step without changing time_to_run. Otherwise, under ag_work_lock, for each index in cb_ctx->guid_indexes: for a DELETE request it clears the retry schedule when the stored value is already MLX4_GUID_FOR_DELETE_VAL (the SM response is not stored) and otherwise marks the index declined; for a SET request it marks the index declined when the SM response is MLX4_NOT_SET_GUID or when the stored value is nonzero and differs from the response, and otherwise stores the SM response in the record (also calling mlx4_set_admin_guid when the stored value was zero) and clears the retry schedule. A declined index gets a retry delay of 1 second if it was 0, else twice its value capped at 60, and the smallest delay is kept. If any index was declined or the record still has indexes that were not applied, time_to_run is set to now plus that smallest delay (0 if nothing was declined); otherwise the record status becomes MLX4_GUID_INFO_STATUS_SET. It then releases the lock and notifies the slaves with mlx4_ib_notify_slaves_on_guid_change. At the common exit, under going_down_lock and ag_work_lock, it requeues the port's alias_guid_work after the delay from get_low_record_time_index unless the device is going down, and then frees cb_ctx and removes it from the callback list when cb_ctx->sa_query is set, otherwise completes cb_ctx->done.
note: reviewer (round 15) right: for a DELETE whose stored value is already the delete value the response is not stored, only the retry schedule is cleared (old prose blurred that); rounds 1 and 2 (status error/block mismatch skip, first decline sets retry 1, unset-only resched delay 0) are reflected. alias_GUID.c:287-436.

name: mlx4_ib_rereg_user_mr
prose: Precondition: mr is a valid mlx4_ib MR, flags is a combination of IB_MR_REREG_TRANS, IB_MR_REREG_PD and IB_MR_REREG_ACCESS, and the caller serialises this call against mlx4_ib_dereg_mr. Postcondition: it returns NULL on success (the existing MR stays the same) and ERR_PTR(err) on failure. It returns ERR_PTR of the error of ib_umem_check_rereg or of mlx4_mr_hw_get_mpt without further effects. Otherwise it modifies the retrieved MPT entry: IB_MR_REREG_PD changes the PD number (mlx4_mr_hw_change_pd); IB_MR_REREG_ACCESS returns -EPERM if writable access is requested for an umem that is not writable and otherwise changes the access (mlx4_mr_hw_change_access); IB_MR_REREG_TRANS cleans the old translation (mlx4_mr_rereg_mem_cleanup), releases the old umem, obtains a new umem with mlx4_get_umem_mr (on failure mmr->umem is set to NULL), calls mlx4_mr_rereg_mem_write and mlx4_ib_umem_write_mtt, releasing the new umem when either fails (the mmr->umem pointer is not cleared then) and updating mmr->mmr.iova and size after the first. Failures in these steps jump to the exit with the error and with earlier steps (for example a PD or access change) not rolled back. Finally it writes the MPT back with mlx4_mr_hw_write_mpt and, only if that succeeds and IB_MR_REREG_ACCESS was set, updates mmr->access_flags and mmr->mmr.access. Every path after a successful mlx4_mr_hw_get_mpt ends with mlx4_mr_hw_put_mpt.
note: reviewer (round 15) is wrong: success returns NULL, not mr (mlx4/mr.c:202-298, 'return NULL' at the end); reviewer round 1 right that earlier PD/access changes are not rolled back when a later step fails. Old prose also claimed the HCA is untouched before the final write, which is not shown by this function.

name: __mlx4_ib_modify_qp
prose: Precondition: src is an ib_qp, or an ib_wq when src_type is MLX4_IB_RWQ_SRC, with an mlx4_ib_qp driver object; attr, attr_mask, cur_state and new_state describe the requested transition. Postcondition: it returns -ENOTSUPP if IB_QP_ALT_PATH is requested on an Ethernet port and -ENOMEM if the QP context cannot be allocated. It then builds the mlx4 QP context from the attributes and calls mlx4_qp_modify. Many validation failures (for example an invalid path MTU, a reserved QKEY, an invalid alternate port or pkey index, a failed mlx4_set_path or mlx4_set_alt_path) jump to the out label without assigning err, so the function returns whatever err held: -EINVAL, its initial value, unless an earlier call (create_qp_lb_counter or rdma_read_gid_l2_fields) had set it to 0, in which case the function can return 0 although the context was not applied. Other failures assign the error explicitly (create_qp_lb_counter, rdma_read_gid_l2_fields, handle_eth_ud_smac_index and undefined RoCE mode give -EINVAL where noted in the code) and the error from mlx4_qp_modify is returned. On success qp->state, the cached access flags, resp_depth, port, alt_port and SQP attributes are updated, QP0 port init or close is done for QP0 transitions, and for a transition to RESET the CQ entries are cleaned and the kernel QP's queue pointers and registered MAC/VLAN state are reset. At out, if err is nonzero it frees the QP counter (when set) and the steering registration, it frees the context, and it commits (success) or unregisters (failure) the candidate source MAC and VLAN of the primary and alternate paths; it returns err.
note: reviewer (round 15) is right: mlx4_set_path and the other bare 'goto out' checks keep err unchanged, so after a successful create_qp_lb_counter or rdma_read_gid_l2_fields call (err = 0) they return 0; rounds 1 and 2 (partial state, set_path not propagated) are consistent. mlx4/qp.c:2117-2700.

name: parse_flow_attr
prose: Precondition: mdev, spec, ib_spec, flow_attr and action are valid and spec's match criteria and match value buffers are allocated. Postcondition: it selects on the type of ib_spec (ignoring the inner flag) and writes the corresponding mlx5 match criteria and match value fields into spec->match_criteria and spec->match_value (Ethernet, IPv4, IPv6, TCP, UDP, GRE, MPLS and VXLAN specs), or sets the flow action (tag, drop, handle, count) in action or spec->flow_context. It returns 0 on success; -EOPNOTSUPP for specs or fields the device cannot match on (for example IB_FLOW_SPEC_ESP always, or a spec whose capability is missing); -EINVAL for an invalid field combination or an unknown spec type (default case); and the error of the action-handle parser for IB_FLOW_SPEC_ACTION_HANDLE. On an error return the match buffers may be partly written.
note: slice cut the head; packet name parse_flow_spec does not exist, the function is parse_flow_attr (mlx5/fs.c:189-541). The earlier drop was wrong; prose is a summary verified against the return statements of the switch.

name: mlx5r_add_gid_macsec_operations
prose: Precondition: attr is a valid GID attribute for an mlx5 IB device. Postcondition: it returns 0 without any change when attr->gid_type is not IB_GID_TYPE_ROCE_UDP_ENCAP, when MACsec RoCE is unsupported, or when the netdev is not an offloaded MACsec device; it returns -ENODEV if attr->ndev is NULL. Otherwise it holds the netdev, takes dev->macsec.lock, and returns -ENOMEM if get_macsec_device fails. It looks up the physical GID with rdma_find_gid; if found, it calls set_roce_addr on it (on error it puts the GID attribute, cleans up the macsec device and returns the error) and records it in the port's reserved_gids. It then adds the RoCE steering rules with mlx5_macsec_add_roce_rule. If that fails and a physical GID was found, it restores the physical GID address, resets macsec_index to -1, puts the GID attribute, cleans up the macsec device and returns the error. If it fails and no physical GID was found, it still saves the RoCE GID with mlx5_macsec_save_roce_gid and returns the nonzero error without calling cleanup_macsec_device. On success it saves the RoCE GID, and returns 0, keeping the physical GID reference in reserved_gids. The netdev reference is released and the mutex dropped on every path after they were taken.
note: reviewer (round 15) is right: an add_roce_rule failure with no physical GID returns the error without cleanup_macsec_device (macsec.c:218-263). Slice cut the head (function starts at line 218).
